record.title: SEMV reports improved multimedia verification and safer reuse of corrected cases
record.summary: The authors introduce SEMV, a multi-agent multimedia verification system that represents evidence as provenance-bearing support and attack arguments, routes human corrections to affected stages, and gates memory reuse through verification and conflict retention. On the 1,700-record COSMOS test set, the Qwen3.6 variant reports 91.88% accuracy versus 89.10% for the strongest directly comparable full-test baseline (unpaired two-proportion z-test p=0.006); other backbones show smaller or nonsignificant differences. In a Qwen memory ablation, unrestricted updates show 5.7% negative transfer, versus 0.2% when verification and conflict retention are added. The authors also report 96.7% correction of initial errors and 52.8% compute savings in a constructed contestation benchmark. These are author-reported results: COSMOS is controlled binary image-caption consistency, MV2026 evaluates only 10 validation and 10 private-test cases, and the 50 CTR episodes come from 10 independent source cases. No independent reproduction was conducted.
organizations: University of Science and Technology of Hanoi

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On COSMOS full test (n=1,700), the authors report Qwen3.6 SEMV accuracy of 91.88% versus 89.10% for the strongest directly comparable full-test baseline; the paper reports an unpaired two-proportion z-test p=0.006.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In the Qwen3.6 memory ablation, the authors report negative transfer of 5.7% with unrestricted memory updates and 0.2% after adding verified consolidation and conflict retention.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_LIMITATION
claims.text: The paper states COSMOS is controlled binary image-caption consistency; MV2026 includes 10 validation and 10 private-test cases, and CTR has 50 episodes from 10 independent source cases. These evaluations do not establish open-world professional fact-checking effectiveness.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction or audit of the author-run COSMOS results and memory ablation was performed.
Generalization to open-world professional verification and independently adjudicated longitudinal corrections is not established.

brief.importance_rationale: If verification systems can preserve evidence provenance, route corrections causally, and reuse prior cases without harmful transfer, they could improve scalable multimedia fact-checking. The reported gains are promising but bounded by controlled datasets and small contestation cases.
limitations: Author-reported preprint results; no independent reproduction was conducted.
COSMOS is a controlled binary image-caption consistency benchmark, not open-world fact-checking.
MV2026 has 10 validation and 10 private-test cases; CTR has 50 episodes derived from 10 independent source cases.
The compared improvements vary across backbones; the Gemma4 accuracy difference is not statistically significant in the paper's test.
organizations: University of Science and Technology of Hanoi

technical.claimed_result: The authors report 91.88% COSMOS accuracy for the Qwen3.6 variant versus a 89.10% directly comparable baseline and, in the Qwen memory ablation, 0.2% negative transfer with verified consolidation plus conflict retention versus 5.7% with unrestricted updates.
technical.demonstrated_result: The arXiv paper documents the SEMV design and its author-run evaluations. It does not independently establish the reported gains, open-world fact-checking effectiveness or deployment benefit.
technical.mechanism: SEMV encodes evidence and claims as provenance-bearing support and attack arguments, routes human contestations to affected pipeline stages, and consolidates candidate memories only after provenance, support, duplication and conflict checks.
technical.regime: Author-run evaluation on COSMOS binary image-caption consistency (full test n=1,700), a very small MV2026 evaluation and a constructed contestation-trace revision set with 50 episodes from 10 source cases.
technical.reproducibility: No independent replication or code/data audit was conducted in this activation.
technical.strongest_baseline: For the full COSMOS test, the authors compare against the directly comparable Tran et al. baseline at 89.10%; the paper uses an unpaired two-proportion z-test because baseline record-level predictions are unavailable.

brief.title: SEMV reports improved multimedia verification and safer reuse of corrected cases
brief.why_it_matters: Evidence provenance, localized correction and safe reuse of prior cases are central to dependable multimedia verification. SEMV offers a concrete integrated design and reports controlled gains, while its small open-world and contestation evaluations leave effectiveness in professional fact-checking uncertain.
